QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_49

question.text: A Logic Model differs from a Theory of Change primarily in that:

answer.text: Logic Model is more linear and visual (input-activity-output-outcome diagram); ToC is more narrative, emphasises assumptions, causal pathways and context
Logic Model is mandatory under SAS-100; ToC is optional
Logic Model was invented in India; ToC is a foreign concept
Logic Model can only be used for environmental projects

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 6 comparison table: Logic Model uses a linear, sequential diagram focused on internal program components (inputs → activities → outputs → outcomes). ToC is narrative-driven, emphasises the causal pathway, explicitly tests assumptions, and considers external context. Many SEs use a combination to capture strengths of each. The Trap: Neither is mandated by SAS-100 uniquely. Both are international tools. Both are sector-agnostic. Cross-Exam Context: XXIII Ch 5 (ToC deep dive) and Ch 6 comparison table both test this distinction — expect recurring questions on the pairing. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When the SE has a slick Logic Model but weak assumption disclosure, insist on a ToC overlay session — it's the single highest-value addition you can make in the planning phase of an SIA engagement.
